honors.title: We Can Award
honors.description:
Internal award for going beyond the mark to improve company products

"Cam has driven improvements around Accessibility in Workspaces, making aspects of Workspaces increasingly accessible via screen readers by visually impaired users of our products. Cam did significant research on his own time around Accessibility needs and requirements of various organizations, then evangelized the need to do this work with his teammates and mentored them while they helped him with the work.
The passion Cam has demonstrated in this area is indicative of a developer who wants to resolve technical debt before it becomes a limiting factor to our business. In time, a Workspaces solution which meets Accessibility requirements set by government institutions will enable our products to be sold to customers we otherwise would not be able to reach."

projects.title: Analyzing Relationships Between United States Section 508 Web Accessibility Guidelines and Usability of Internet Content
projects.description:
ABSTRACT 
This research examines the Section 508 amendment of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, which creates web accessibility standards, implemented by the United States federal government to ascertain their impact on usability for disabled and non-disabled users.  Though users with and without disabilities have different needs, it is widely thought that accessibility and usability are correlated.  This research seeks to understand the relationships which exist between accessibility, as measured by Section 508 Guidelines, and usability.  Additionally, this research assesses the usability impact of various web content types, namely text; video; audio; images; forms; infographics; and tables, when accessibility guidelines are applied.  
This research finds that usability for both disabled and non-disabled users can be significantly improved through compliance with Section 508 guidelines, across almost all web content types studied.  However, several caveats hinder drastic improvements for several content types and sizeable room remains for rulemakers, standards bodies, and web browsers to better clarify guidelines and implement accessible native HTML elements.
